## What you’ll see in Colombia

High in the Andes, Bogotá pairs the colonial architecture of its old quarters with modern neighbourhoods, cafés, restaurants and museums. Get to know Colombia’s history through the city’s squares and churches, the Gold Museum and the Botero Museum, then take in the city panorama from Monserrate.

In the Coffee Region, green valleys and plantations take the place of city streets. The Cocora Valley is home to wax palms, Colombia’s national tree. At Hacienda Venecia, you can follow coffee from plantation to cup and take part in some stages of processing the beans.

The trip ends in Cartagena, with sea air and the architecture of the old city. Fortified walls surround the historic centre, and the itinerary takes in the Castillo San Felipe de Barajas, the city’s churches and the convent on Cerro de la Popa. After travelling through the Andes and the Coffee Region, you’ll have a full day free in Cartagena to explore or relax as you like.
